text:
sam.sales: Hey team — Acme is ready for a short POC this week (Wed-Fri). They want a Private deployment: either connect to our hosted Private endpoint via an interface endpoint (Privatelink/VPCE) or set up VPC peering to our transit VPC. Questions from them: can we provide a hosted API key for initial smoke tests, what subnets/route entries do they need, and any quick security constraints?

tasha_engineering: I’d recommend VPCE (interface endpoint) for the POC — lower blast radius and no route-table peering changes. Quick checklist: private subnets in at least 2 AZs, SG allowing outbound 443 to our VPCE ENIs, enable Private DNS on the endpoint so the SDK resolves our service domain to the VPCE. :white_check_mark:

leo_infra: Adding infra notes — if they insist on VPC peering (they have legacy constraints), they need:
- Peer created (accept on our side)
- Route table entry in their VPC: dest = our service CIDR (e.g., 10.200.0.0/16) -> target = pcx-xxxx
- Route table entry in our side (if cross-account) back to their CIDR
- Security groups allow traffic between CIDRs
But peering won't give them our Private DNS automatically, they'd need to manage hostnames or use a shared resolver.

julie_devops: Quick example SG + endpoint CLI for VPCE setup we often share with customers:
```bash
# create endpoint (customer runs in their account)
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \\n  --vpc-id vpc-012345 \\n  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-zzzzzz \\n  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \\n  --subnet-ids subnet-1a subnet-1b \\n  --security-group-ids sg-0abc1234\\n  --private-dns-enabled
```
Security group (example):
```text
Ingress: TCP 443 from 10.0.0.0/8 (customer app CIDR)
Egress: TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 (or narrower if you require)
```
Share that snippet and ask them to enable private DNS — otherwise SDK will hit public hostnames.

karen_security: Policy/security notes: do NOT hand out long-lived hosted API keys that are account-global for POCs. Options:
- Provide a time-limited token scoped to customer (we can issue ephemeral creds + short TTL)
- If they need service account keys, rotate and store in their KMS, provide limited scope and alerting
Also confirm whether traffic must go through their FW/NAT. For interface endpoints traffic stays within AWS network, but if they route via NAT gateway for egress e.g., to our hosted control plane, document that.

sam.sales: Good — they asked specifically about DNS: "If we enable Private DNS does our service domain resolve automatically to vpce ENIs?" and whether they should change their route tables.

tasha_engineering: Yes — when Private DNS is enabled on the interface endpoint, the regional service domain (e.g., api.redwood-inference.internal) resolves to the VPCE ENIs in their VPC. No route table changes needed for the endpoint itself. Only make route changes if using VPC peering.

leo_infra: Also watch out for cross-account endpoint service setup if we host in a separate account — we need to grant acceptance and potentially whitelist their account id for the service. If we expect >1 AZ, ensure they place the VPCE in subnets across those AZs.

sam.sales: They also asked about Dedicated pool vs Private network: if they plan sustained throughput (>X RPS) should we recommend Dedicated?

julie_devops: For POC, VPCE -> hosted private endpoint is quickest. If they plan steady high throughput and want isolation, propose Dedicated pool with a reserved commit. We should include cost estimate in the POC quote — I'll create a short appendix.

karen_security: One more ask from legal: we need an architecture diagram and an ACL list for audit. I'll send a template. For keys we'll accept ephemeral tokens only for the POC.

ops_bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpce-poc-checklist — contains sample SG, RT, DNS notes, and acceptance template.

sam.sales: Action items: 
1) Julie: prepare a short cost appendix and a Dedicated vs Hosted-PVCE comparison (today)
2) Tasha/Leo: provide the VPCE CLI snippet + confirm if we need to whitelist their account id (ASAP)
3) Karen: send the security artifact template to Acme and confirm ephemeral token flow (today)
4) I’ll coordinate times for Wed for initial smoke once they confirm subnets

julie_devops: On it — will drop the appendix in this thread when ready. :rocket:

tasha_engineering: FYI if they run into DNS caching issues, instruct them to flush resolver cache or restart app pods — common POC snag.

sam.sales: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for the handshake. ping me if blockers. :thumbsup:
